slug: 2023-01-01 Digital Trade Regulatory Integration - Namibia Country Profile

facts.fact: The UNECA country profile states that Namibia's Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 came into force in March 2021 and covers electronic signatures, consumer protection and contracts; the document carries no date of its own, so its published year 2023 is the proxy for the report.

New Era reports that the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 and its accreditation regulations were the basis on which CRAN accredited the Ministry of Home Affairs as a certification service provider (announced on an unnamed Tuesday of the week of the 3 September 2026 article).

CRAN accredited the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security as Namibia's first Certification Service Provider under the Act and its accreditation regulations, valid four years; the article dates it only as Tuesday, so the week of its 3 September 2026 publication is used.

systems.tiers: Ministry of Home Affairs electronic identity system linked by key signing ceremony on 28 August 2026

facts.fact: Observer24 reports that Section 20 and Chapter 5 of the Electronic Transactions Act, giving the legal framework for electronic signatures, came into operation on 15 June 2026.

systems.tiers: national; banks, telecommunications companies and government institutions expected to adopt
top of national digital trust chain; oversees accredited certification service providers

facts.fact: Government Notice 335 in Gazette 8814 records Minister Theofelus making the Electronic Signature Regulations under section 20 of the Electronic Transactions Act, 2019, signed 27 November 2025 and published 19 December 2025, to commence with section 20 of the Act.

General Notice 953 in Gazette 8808 records CRAN making regulations on accreditation of security products and services and certification service providers under sections 41 to 47 of the Electronic Transactions Act, 2019, published 17 December 2025, to commence on a date the Chairperson sets by gazette notice.
facts.system: Regulations regarding Accreditation of Security Products and Services and Providers of such Products and Services

facts.fact: CRAN's Regulations regarding Accreditation of Security Products and Services (General Notice 953 of 17 December 2025) were made under Chapter 5 of the Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019, covering application, issue, renewal and revocation of certification service provider accreditation.
The Act's Chapter 5 and these regulations came into force on 15 June 2026 via General Notice 182/2026.

note: Article says government is preparing legally recognised e-signatures by February 2026 and working on provider accreditation; it does not state the Act's commencement or any rules made, so no fact (published 2025-09-17).

facts.fact: The Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019, signed by the President on 7 November 2019, was promulgated in Government Gazette 7068 (Government Notice 364) on 29 November 2019; it covers legal recognition of data messages, electronic signatures, contracts, consumer protection and accreditation of security services; the excerpt does not give the commencement date.

Market Watch reports the DigiNam launch on 31 August 2026 followed implementation of provisions of the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019, which it says provides the legal basis for electronic signatures, trust services and accreditation of certification service providers.

facts.fact: The Economist (Namibia) reports Chapter 5 and Section 20 of the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 came into effect in June 2026.

The Economist (Namibia) reports DigiNam was launched on 31 August 2026 under the Act, with CRAN serving as Root Certification Authority tasked with accrediting certification service providers; no accreditation is yet reported.

systems.owner: CRAN as Root CA, with Ministries of Home Affairs and ICT

facts.fact: The ICT minister writes that the Electronic Transactions Act, 2019 recognizes electronic transactions and signatures, and that the e-ID complements it.

NAM-CSIRT's 2025 report has a section on secured electronic signature accreditation under the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019, which gives electronic signatures the same legal weight as handwritten ones; the report carries no date of issue, so its published date is used.
The report states CRAN is operationalising regulations under the Act on secured electronic signature accreditation; the report carries no date of issue, so its published date is used.
The ICT minister said the government would launch electronic signatures in February 2026 under the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019, carrying the same legal weight as handwritten signatures.
The ICT minister said electronic signatures would be introduced by February 2026 under the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019, giving them the same legal standing as handwritten signatures.

The Legal Assistance Centre's annotated text says the Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 (GG 7068), signed by the President on 7 November 2019, was brought into force on 16 March 2020 by GN 75/2020 (GG 7142), except section 20 (electronic signatures), Chapter 4 (consumer protection) and Chapter 5 (accreditation of security services).

The annotated text says section 20 (recognised electronic signatures) and Chapter 5 (accreditation of security products and services by the Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia) of the Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 were brought into force on 15 June 2026 by GN 182/2026 (GG 8949); the chapter on online consumer protection (Chapter 4) is annotated as not yet in force.

facts.fact: The Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia's Mufaro Nesongano said Namibia's Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 provides a legal framework for electronic agreements and signatures, subject to applicable requirements.
The Villager lists the electronic transactions act among the laws Namibia has in place, besides the cybercrime bill, in its report on the MICT stakeholder engagement.

CRAN published regulations on accreditation of security products and services and their providers under the Electronic Transactions Act 2019 (General Notice 953, 17 December 2025), and on 15 June 2026 determined they commence with section 20 and Part 5 of the Act.

facts.fact: TechReviewAfrica reports Namibia has legally recognised electronic signatures, allowing businesses and public institutions to conclude contracts and submit trade documents electronically, but names no instrument.

note: No law named; only says PKI enables legally recognised e-signatures, no law or draft stated.
